facts.text: The Test Pier Fountain was built in 1732 and carries a carved verse inscription.
Its water came down from a hillside spring through clay pipes.
The Test Library was founded in 1740 by the patron named in the fountain's verse.
The Test Bathhouse was fed by the same hillside spring as the fountain.
The Test Guild Hall carries the patron's crest and was a guild hall for tile makers.
The Test Arcade has 12 marble arches carved by the same workshop as the bathhouse lions.
The Test Observatory was the patron's last gift, opened in 1761.
The observatory dome is tiled by the guild of tile makers and edged with marble from the arcade's quarry.

writer.title: The Patron's Last Gift

mystery.question: What was the patron's last gift to these streets?
mystery.answer: The observatory on the hill, opened in 1761.

writer.briefing: One patron paid for half of what you will see today. Find his last gift. Stay on the pavement, daylight only.
